title: Getting DRG neurons into a dish
objective: Explain why and how DRG neurons are dissociated into culture.

steps.title: One ganglion, many cells
steps.body: One common way to study single sensory neurons: dissect **[[DRG]]**, then use enzymes to make a **[[dissociated culture]]** — the ganglion broken into individual cell bodies in a dish. Now each neuron is accessible for calcium imaging or patch recording.

steps.prompt: Why dissociate the DRG instead of imaging it intact?
options: To access and record from individual neuron cell bodies
To use GCaMP, which only works in cultured neurons
To make the sensory neurons divide and multiply again
To let the neurons regrow the axons cut during dissection
steps.explanation: Dissociation separates the tightly packed cell bodies so you can study and stimulate them one at a time.

variants.setup: You want to patch single DRG neurons and give every cell body direct drug access.
variants.reveal: A dish of separated cell bodies lets you image and stimulate each neuron individually.

steps.setup: Culture makes DRG neurons easy to reach and image.
steps.prompt: What's a limitation of cultured DRG neurons?
options: They lose their normal connections and tissue context
They keep dividing in culture, so their numbers drift
They can no longer fire an action potential at all
steps.reveal: Culture is powerful for access but artificial: the neuron is cut from its endings and partners, so some properties change. Pair it with in vivo work.

variants.prompt: A caveat of dissociated DRG culture is that neurons…
variants.explanation: Removed from tissue, their context and some properties change.

reviewNotes: DRG dissociation; sets up calcium imaging.
